### Phase 4: in-pipeline scene classifier + SceneLighting fusion, backlit first

`active` · `@raw-autotune.work.phase-4-backlit-scene-lighting-wiring/1`

### Slice 8 — Sky stage attribution and local-tone/HDR evaluation

`active` · `@raw-autotune.work.slice-8-local-tone-sky-ground-hdr-evaluation/5`

Attribute the visible sky failure to an exact pipeline boundary before changing the default render. Keep the existing local-tone and HDR evaluations for scene-luminance compression, but do not use either operator to conceal a colour-estimation discontinuity.

Add renderer-exact, lossless diagnostic checkpoints after the tone curve, chroma scale, highlight white mix, and gamut compression. The normal render and the final diagnostic checkpoint must share one implementation and remain byte-identical. On `_DSC1289.ARW`, compare the default against reconstruction disabled, `--local-tone 0.35`, and `--hdr 0.5`; measure adjacent OKLab chroma steps across raw clip-state boundaries and within the same clip state.

The current attribution found that reconstruction introduces clip-cohort plateaus and that the max-channel-weighted tone shoulder is the main discontinuity amplifier. Local tone and HDR do not repair the colour estimate, gamut compression is effectively inactive in the measured sky, and the peak-preserving path toward white reduces rather than creates the boundary. Continue evaluating local tone/HDR only after the reconstruction estimator and its end-to-end ground-truth bench can distinguish recovered detail from invented colour.

### Candidate D: calibrated camera-profile hue/saturation table where matrix colour is insufficient

`proposed` · `@raw-autotune.work.calibrated-hue-sat-table-candidate-d/1`

Evaluate and, if justified, implement a DCP-style hue/saturation lookup table applied after the colour matrix, per Candidate D of docs/PURPLE_SKY_PROBLEM_SCOPE.md and its acceptance gates. This is the full closure path for the residual look gap between our faithful matrix rendering of bright blue-violet sky and the camera JPEG, now that decision.faithful-blue-violet-sky-over-camera-white-shoulder keeps the default shoulder unchanged.

Prerequisite that blocks implementation today: calibrated table data. Either a colour-chart plus sky-bracket capture on the user's Sony body, or a licensing-and-attribution review of an existing profile source (Adobe DCP tables; Darktable/RawTherapee GPL data would need explicit review even under our AGPL-3.0-or-later). No code change is warranted before one of those exists.

First steps when picked up: settle the data source, then prototype the table as a default-disabled flag with the scope document's gates (held-out Sony set, no neutralisation of legitimate saturated blues or sunsets, determinism across worker counts, memory-planner inclusion).
